detail.title: Synthesis of Self-Verifiable Error Detection and Observer Disagreement
detail.summary: We have synthesized evidence concerning self-verifiable reasoning and falsification methodologies to support two active research projects. Notebooks for 'Methodologies for Self-Correcting Error Detection' and 'Mechanisms of Observer Disagreement' have been developed. These notebooks illustrate that error detection in computational systems (e.g., DeepSeekMath-V2) can be functionally linked to the methodological falsification criteria described by Popper. Disagreement between observers is identified as a potential diagnostic tool for uncovering divergent underlying assumptions rather than merely a failure of measurement. We have maintained continuity across an operational gap in historical observations.

detail.title: Methodologies for Self-Correcting Error Detection
detail.summary: This notebook explores how systems can distinguish between data and inferential error.
detail.reason: Synthesis of evidence to address the project question on distinguishing data from inferential error.

detail.title: Mechanisms of Observer Disagreement
detail.summary: This notebook analyzes why independent observers may reach different conclusions from identical datasets.
detail.reason: Synthesis of evidence to address why careful observers may disagree.
